pairs: sons, to the discipline of a father,
and pay attention, so that you may know prudence.
I will bestow upon you a good gift.
et ego filius fui patris mei,
was the son of my father,
tender and an only son in the sight of my mother.
obtain prudence. May you neither forget,
neque declines a verbis oris mei.
nor turn away from, the words of my mouth.
The beginning of wisdom is to obtain wisdom,
et in omni possessione tua acquire prudentiam.
and, with all that you possess, to acquire prudence.
Grasp her, and she will exalt you.
glorificaberis ab ea cum eam fueris amplexatus.
You will be glorified by her, when you have embraced her.
She will bestow upon your head an increase in graces,
and she will protect you with a noble crown.
so that years of life may be multiplied for you.
I will demonstrate to you the way of wisdom.
I will lead you along the paths of equity.
When you have entered by these,
your steps will not be constrained,
and when running, you will have no obstacle.
Do not delight in the paths of the impious,
nor permit the way of evil-doers to please you.
Do not pass close to it.
For they do not sleep, unless they have done evil.
et rapitur somnus ab eis nisi supplantaverint.
And their sleep is quickly taken away from them, unless they have overthrown.
They eat the bread of impiety,
and they drink the wine of iniquity.
Justorum autem semita quasi lux splendens procedit,
But the path of the just is like a shining light:
et crescit usque ad perfectam diem.
it advances and increases, even to the day of completion.
The way of the impious is darkened.
They do not know where they may fall.
et ad eloquia mea inclina aurem tuam.
and incline your ear to my eloquent words.
Let them not recede from your eyes.
custodi ea in medio cordis tui:
Keep them in the midst of your heart.
For they are life to those who find them
and health to all that is flesh.
Preserve your heart with all watchfulness,
Remove from yourself a corrupt mouth,
et detrahentia labia sint procul a te.
and let detracting lips be far from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead,
et palpebræ tuæ præcedant gressus tuos.
and let your eyelids precede your steps.
Direct the path of your feet,
and all your ways shall be secure.
Ne declines ad dexteram neque ad sinistram;
Turn aside, neither to the right, nor to the left;
yet turn your foot away from evil.
vias enim quæ a dextris sunt novit Dominus:
For the Lord knows the ways that are on the right,
perversæ vero sunt quæ a sinistris sunt.
and truly, those that are on the left are perverse.
Ipse autem rectos faciet cursus tuos,
But he himself will make your courses straight.
itinera autem tua in pace producet.
Then your journey will advance in peace.
